entries.subject: OpenSpace Milky Way volume
entries.finding: The galaxy is the lossless 1024 x 1024 x 128 RGBA density grid adapted by OpenSpace from a NAOJ simulation prepared by Jon Parker for AMNH's Dark Universe, declared MIT with the original notice preserved; the README states it is a scientific simulation adapted for visualization, not a measured map of our galaxy's exact shape, and the source already contains its bulge.

entries.subject: Channel transfer and optical coefficients from the source recipe
entries.finding: RGB channels emit independently after squaring filtered UNORM values and alpha is dust decoded with exponent 1.4; the recipe preserves emission 250, absorption 200, extinction tint 0.3/0.54/0.85, cylindrical support and the source's channel transfer, converting the 8 kpc Galactic centre and authored Euler rotation into the shared Sun-centred ICRF frame.

entries.subject: CSS display gain after slab integration
entries.finding: The display gain is calibrated to 16 after slab integration, three stops below the previous 128 baseline that was too bright with the OpenSpace emission model; these are renderer approximation choices kept separate from OpenSpace's authored emission and absorption coefficients.

entries.subject: Offline display-RGB grading matrix toward the NASA palette
entries.finding: A single offline matrix diag(1, 0.951277424, 0.709752511) grades every slab toward the original NASA interior palette from every viewing direction, following the exponential transfer and preserving emission and dust alpha; calibrated on paired patches within 15 degrees of the Galactic plane with held-out longitude blocks, it reduces held-out chromaticity error by 53.8 percent while retaining colour variation, and matches the palette rather than morphology or physical photometry.

entries.subject: OpenSpace additive HDR raymarching and stochastic sampling
entries.finding: Ordinary-alpha slices approximate RGB extinction and emitted energy, retain finite-slice and axis-handoff artefacts and do not reproduce OpenSpace's additive HDR raymarching, stochastic sampling or camera-dependent fade.
entries.revisitWhen: A prepared route reproduces additive HDR raymarching within the project's rendering rules.

entries.subject: NASA Deep Star Maps 2020 Milky Way-only celestial map
entries.finding: The near-Solar-System sky uses the 8192 x 4096 linear RGB HALF source in ICRF/J2000, preserved bit for bit in two Zstd row chunks with its acquisition record, hashes and NASA/Gaia credits; the offline baker applies a fixed 4.5 exposure and the sRGB curve, matching NASA's preview mean RGB within 0.001 with RGB RMSE 0.01387 before a final 0.12 display gain, which the README calls a display fit rather than calibrated photometry.

entries.subject: Smooth shadow factor over faint sky pixels
entries.finding: A shared smooth shadow factor suppresses faint image grain, zero below transferred display luminance 0.04 and full above 0.12, intentionally removing faint background detail while retaining the separately baked catalogue stars; faint Gaia stars remain in the image, so it is not literally star-free.

entries.subject: Neighbourhood star field baked into the near cube faces
entries.finding: The baker composites the sibling stellar-neighbourhood point field, pinned by descriptor digest at an authored 43.6 CSS pixels per degree, onto a copy of each face: about 17,500 sprites drawn with the same atlas tile, photometry table and source-over blend the browser uses, supersampled three times per axis; the NASA Milky Way-only image omits bright Hipparcos and Tycho stars, so the prepared bright stars are composited in.

entries.subject: Per-star DOM starfield and its parallax
entries.finding: The runtime mounts only the baked faces: there is no 100 AU handoff to individual DOM stars, star-slot pool, catalogue-selection worker or per-star frame transport, so individual stellar parallax is no longer rendered and a star's disc is about three times softer than the browser's own sprite at device pixel ratio 2, which the README calls a deliberate visual difference.
entries.revisitWhen: The project decides that per-star parallax inside the neighbourhood is worth the runtime star transport again.

entries.subject: Depth of the prepared sky shell
entries.finding: The 20 kpc half-extent shell depth is an authored visual approximation because NASA supplies angular radiance, not measured cloud depths; it aligns neither source's dust structure nor reproduces physical disocclusion, and it avoids copying cloud features across independent depth layers.
entries.revisitWhen: A source supplies measured cloud depths that can replace the authored shell.
